the use of bisophosphonates in prostate cancer patients with bone metastasis is not recommended, but that the use of these agents in patients with prostate cancer who do not have bone metastases is not recommended.

we have demonstrated that bisphosphonate therapy is effective for the treatment of bone metastases in prostate cancer patients.
we have shown that bisphosphonate therapy in patients with metastatic prostate cancer is associated with significant improvements in skeletal-related events and overall survival.

bisphosphonate use is associated with a reduced risk of prostate cancer progression, and this association appears to be independent of the type of bisphosphate.
